t: This is the Finborough Theatre in West Brompton, a tiny fifty-seat theatre under artistic director Neil McPherson. It's known for new British writing, premieres of plays in translation and from across the English-speaking world, and rarely seen plays from the nineteenth and twentieth centuries. It also stages new and rediscovered music theatre. The building was designed by George Godwin, an influential architect who also edited The Builder magazine. The Scottish actor Gordon Reid died here, a reminder that this small room has a real place in the lives of working actors.
